title: finding(docs): the VS Code page's keybinding example rebinds Ctrl+Shift+P over the Command Palette in exactly the files the page tells you to use it in
body:
Found while working objectui#8113 (branch `claude/issue-8113-vscode-shortcuts-page`), which corrects that page's false claim that the extension ships default keyboard shortcuts. Two things on the same page are outside that card's fix and are filed here rather than ridden along, because one of them is a chord choice and chord choices are the thing objectui#8113 is explicitly fenced away from.

## 1. The worked keybinding example shadows the Command Palette

`content/docs/utilities/vscode-extension.mdx`, the `Bind a command yourself` section, shows this as the way to bind a command:

```json
{
  "key": "ctrl+shift+p",
  "command": "objectui.preview",
  "when": "editorLangId == json"
}
```

`ctrl+shift+p` is VS Code's default for `workbench.action.showCommands`. With `when: editorLangId == json` this entry wins inside JSON editors — which is precisely where an ObjectUI schema is open, and precisely where the same page (twice: the `Commands` intro and the `Open Preview` usage steps) tells the reader to press `Ctrl+Shift+P` to reach the Command Palette. A reader who copies the example loses the route the rest of the page is built on, in the only file type where it matters.

Nothing here is false — it is a valid `keybindings.json` entry — so it is not a correctness fix, which is why objectui#8113 left it byte-identical. It is a foot-gun, and objectui#8113 makes it worse in the sense that the example is now the section's primary instruction rather than an aside under a table of shipped defaults.

Deliberately not fixed in objectui#8113: replacing the key means choosing a chord, and choosing chords for this extension is the separate maintainer decision that objectui#8113's dispatch reserved. The example does not have to name a plausible ObjectUI chord at all — an obviously-illustrative unbound key, or dropping the `when` clause, both defuse it without deciding anything.

## 2. `Object UI: Open Preview to the Side` has no entry in the Commands section

`contributes.commands` lists six commands. The `Commands` section documents five; `objectui.previewToSide` has never had a heading of its own. objectui#8113 added it to that page's command-id table (a complete list read off the manifest is the point of that card), and corrected the `Open Preview` description, which had been describing `previewToSide`'s behaviour — `objectui.preview` calls `showPreview(uri, false)` and lands in `ViewColumn.One`, while `objectui.previewToSide` passes `true` and lands in `ViewColumn.Beside` (`packages/vscode-extension/src/providers/PreviewProvider.ts:25-37`). So the distinction is now drawn on the page but the sixth command still has no `Usage` block like its five siblings.

This is an omission, not a false statement, which is why objectui#8113 did not write one: adding a section is new content, not a correction.

## Neither is caught by anything

Measured on objectui#8113's branch by ablation, with a live control. Re-injecting the deleted `Default keyboard shortcuts:` table into the page leaves all eight doc gates that read `content/docs` at exit 0 (`check-doc-component-types`, `check-doc-fence-languages`, `check-doc-links`, `check-doc-snippet-types`, `check-doc-example-types`, `check-doc-expression-carriage`, `body-dialect-census`, `check-control-bytes`) and all 212 tests in the suites that read this page green. The control that makes that a reading rather than a harness that never fires: mutating `"type": "h1"` to `"type": "heading"` in the same file turns `scripts/__tests__/check-doc-component-types.test.ts` red (exit 1, 2 tests failed) — the harness does read this file and can fail on it. It simply has no comparison between the page's prose and the extension's manifest or sources.

Same cluster as objectui#7976 / objectui#7974 / objectui#7837: a document mirroring something no tool re-derives.

Filed unassigned, no labels, for triage.
